title: Static and Gravity
premise: When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, Hazel Nystrom's cargo hauler is thrown into a debris field near the abandoned seed vault he once tended — and he discovers the flicker was no accident but a weaponized signal test by Meridian Combine, which now controls Earth's last transmission loop. Carrying a stolen data core that proves Meridian engineered the flicker to erase evidence of its orbital massacres, Hazel races toward the dead-space relay where an independent broadcast can expose the truth before the transmission loop resets and buries it forever. Hunted by Meridian enforcers and betrayed by his own navigator, Hazel reaches the relay with minutes left and must choose between broadcasting the truth and saving the crewmate who came back for him. He finds a third path: piggybacking the signal on the seed vault's dormant uplink, exposing Meridian at the cost of the vault itself — and of the identity he built as its caretaker.
about_author: Marguerite Vasquez is a former radio engineer from the Chilean coast who writes science fiction about people who keep machines alive long after institutions abandon them. Her work has appeared in several small-press anthologies exploring labor, memory, and justice at the edges of empire.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Hazel Nystrom, hauling cargo through contested orbits seven years after abandoning his post as seed vault caretaker, experiences the system-wide gravity flicker firsthand when his hauler tumbles through a debris field. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into dread as he realizes the flicker was deliberate — a shaped pulse, not a malfunction.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Ghost
chapters.summary: Hazel docks at Waystation Kettle and finds his old mentor, Ilsa Brandt, waiting with a data core she stole from a Meridian research barge during the nine seconds of chaos. She names him because he knows the vault's frequencies. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: reluctant recognition — the past he buried has come looking for him.

chapters.title: What the Core Remembers
chapters.summary: Decrypted in a rented bay, the core reveals Meridian Combine engineered the flicker to wipe orbital surveillance records of the Callisto Docks massacre. POV: alternating Hazel and the core's archived voice recordings of a dead whistleblower, Ana Reyes. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose; justice will not come from any court.

chapters.title: Crew of Convenience
chapters.summary: Hazel assembles a skeleton crew: navigator Dex Okafor, a charming debt-runner hiding his own agenda; engineer Sunniva 'Sunny' Halvorsen, ex-Meridian and desperate to atone. POV: Sunny. Emotional beat: wary hope — strangers bound by shared guilt rather than trust.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: Meridian security sweeps the station hunting the stolen core; Ilsa stays behind as decoy and is detained. The crew slips the cordon in a cargo launch window measured in minutes. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt layered over old abandonment — he has run before, and knows the taste.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Crossing the inner belt, the crew endures silence, rationing, and Dex's probing questions about what the core contains. Hazel deflects, hoarding the truth like fuel. POV: Dex. Emotional beat: loneliness inside company; Dex begins calculating what betrayal might buy him.

chapters.title: Signal Ghosts
chapters.summary: The hauler picks up fragments of Earth's dying transmission loop — a decades-old broadcast repeating into nothing. Sunny explains Meridian controls the loop's relay chain and plans to let it die quietly, erasing the last unfiltered record of the colonies' founding crimes. POV: Sunny. Emotional beat: horror at how power rewrites history by simply letting it fade.

chapters.title: Ambush at Ceres Shadow
chapters.summary: A Meridian interceptor corners them in Ceres' shadow; Sunny's knowledge of Meridian drone protocols buys an escape through a mining tunnel too narrow for the pursuers. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: first proof that Sunny is worth trusting — and that Meridian knows exactly who carries the core.

chapters.title: The Price of Fuel
chapters.summary: Stranded short of jump range, they barter with a scavver clan led by Old Toma, paying with parts of the ship and a promise. Toma reveals rumors of a dead-space relay still accepting broadcasts outside Meridian's grid. POV: Dex. Emotional beat: the lawless kindness of outsiders — justice lives in the margins.

chapters.title: Dex's Bargain
chapters.summary: In secret, Dex transmits their position to Meridian in exchange for debt forgiveness and safe passage home. He tells himself the crew would never make it anyway. POV: Dex. Emotional beat: self-justification curdling into shame; corruption begins as a small, reasonable trade.

chapters.title: Dead Space Horizon
chapters.summary: They cross into dead space where no patrols fly and the stars feel indifferent. Hazel finally tells the full story of why he abandoned the vault — a Meridian order he obeyed, sealing a contaminated section with workers inside. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: confession as release; his identity as caretaker was always penance.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: They find the relay: ancient, half-dead, maintained by a single hermit technician, Wren, who has kept it broadcasting independent signals for thirty years. But the relay needs a stronger carrier signal than it can generate alone. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet heroism — one person keeping a door open against an empire.

chapters.title: Loop Countdown
chapters.summary: Wren calculates the timing: Earth's transmission loop resets in six days, permanently overwriting the archive band the relay could hijack. They must boost the relay using a transmitter powerful enough — and there is only one such transmitter in the system. POV: Sunny. Emotional beat: hope with a hook in it; she recognizes the frequency profile instantly.

chapters.title: The Vault's Heartbeat
chapters.summary: The only transmitter strong enough belongs to the abandoned seed vault Hazel once tended — Meridian seized it after he left, converting it to a signal hub. Returning means walking into the trap they've prepared. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the past demanding payment; he must reclaim the identity he fled.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Meridian forces board using Dex's coordinates. In the firefight, Dex freezes — then turns his gun on the enforcers instead, buying the crew seconds and taking a wound. POV: Dex. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at blood price; he chooses the crew over his own absolution.

chapters.title: Homecoming to a Lie
chapters.summary: Hazel infiltrates the vault through maintenance shafts he mapped seven years ago, finding it stripped and repurposed — the seeds gone, sold or destroyed. Meridian didn't just take the transmitter; it erased the ark of the old world. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: rage and mourning fused; this is what power does to what it cannot own.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Room
chapters.summary: Sunny and Hazel reach the transmitter core, but Meridian director Cassian Vole appears — not with soldiers, but with an offer: wealth, amnesty, and the loop's survival, if the core is surrendered. He reveals Ilsa died in custody. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: temptation met with cold clarity; Vole offers everything except the one thing that matters.

chapters.title: Gravity Fails Again
chapters.summary: Vole triggers a second localized flicker to disable their escape; in zero-g chaos, Hazel fights through the vault's dark corridors while Sunny reroutes the transmitter feed toward the relay. POV: Sunny. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into competence — the ex-insider dismantling her former masters' machinery.

chapters.title: The Signal Rises
chapters.summary: With the loop reset ninety minutes away, the crew faces the choice: use the vault transmitter to broadcast the evidence, which will burn out the transmitter and doom the vault's remaining systems — including life support for any hidden survivors. Hazel chooses the truth. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: sacrifice without ceremony; justice costs what it costs.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: As the broadcast climbs the relay chain, Meridian launches a final assault on the vault. Wren, remotely patching the relay, holds the connection open while Dex, wounded, mans the defenses. POV: Dex. Emotional beat: three broken people holding one fragile line together — solidarity as the answer to corruption.

chapters.title: Static and Gravity
chapters.summary: The evidence floods every open receiver in the system as the loop resets — Meridian's massacres exposed across a thousand screens. Vole's forces withdraw as his own lieutenants defect. The vault goes dark around them, and Hazel walks out carrying a single surviving seed canister. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: triumph hollowed by loss, then warmed by what remains.

chapters.title: What Grows After
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the crew plants the canister's contents at a free station garden while tribunals — real ones, outside Meridian's reach — convene. Hazel takes a new call sign: not caretaker, not runner, but broadcaster. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: earned peace; identity rebuilt not from what he protected, but from what he refused to let be silenced.
